title: Recusals on record, and matters naming a declared interest
question: When a Board file named an organization from which an official had declared a gift, income or an investment, what does the record show the official did, and how often did a member sit out a single item?
finding: On money files (2015 to 2026, Board and committees), a supervisor is printed Excused on one item while voting on the others that day 25 times (most: Ahsha Safai 5, Shamann Walton 5, Aaron Peskin 3, Mark Farrell 3), and on two to four items 58 times. 43 of those 83 items name an outside organization, and in 3 of them that organization had a money link to the member before the vote (Catherine Stefani and Pacific Gas and Electric: only individual donors who wrote it as their employer, which is the donors’ own text and not money from the company; Shamann Walton and Bay Area Community Resources: a reported source of income or gifts; Shamann Walton and Young Community Developers Inc: a reported source of income or gifts). “Excused” is also printed for a member who is simply out of the room, and a recusal notice on file covers only 1 of the 83 (Ahsha Safai, File 210031). On land-use items the same count is 183 (most: Ahsha Safai 37, Shamann Walton 29, Aaron Peskin 25, Malia Cohen 17), and 1 recusal notice from a supervisor is on file with the Ethics Commission. Against 3,045 declared gifts, income sources and investments, 32 passed Board files name the same organization as counterparty within the declaration period or the twelve months after: 19 follow a gift or travel payment, the largest being travel payment worth $1,679 on 2023-10-09 from Bay Area Community Resources to Shamann Walton before File 240739. The final roll call is now on disk for 32 of the 32 that passed while the official sat on the Board: the member voted yes on 31, no on 0, and was printed Excused on 1 and Absent on 0; 21 of the yes and no votes were on a file naming a reported source of income or gifts, the rest on a file naming a company in which the member reported an investment. None of those files is the subject of a recusal notice by the same official; whether one was required depends on amounts and timing that only the Ethics Commission can rule on.
how: Declared interests are each roster official’s Form 700 gifts and travel payments (Schedules D and E, and the separate Gifts of Travel filings), income sources and business positions (Schedule C) and investments (Schedules A-1 and A-2). Each source name is matched exactly, after removing punctuation and company suffixes, to the counterparty of a contract, grant agreement, lease, loan or settlement file that passed while the official was in office and inside the window: twelve months after a gift, or the reporting period plus twelve months for income and investments. The column “The official’s recorded part” gives what the record shows: sponsor; the vote printed for the member on the file’s final Board passage roll call (money files and lobbied measures, 2015 to 2026, through the shared roll-call reader); a vote on a land-use roll call; or, where no roll call is on disk, simply membership of the Board at the time. Excusals: on each day and in each body, a member counts as excused on an item when the roll calls on disk print “Excused” for that member on that file and an aye or a no on at least one other file. The count takes money files only, counts a member and a file once, and separates a member excused on one file that day from one excused on two to four; five or more files at one meeting are read as leaving the room and are not counted. For each such item that names an outside organization, the member’s money links to it dated before the vote are looked up: the donor circle (the organization or donors naming it as employer giving to the member’s committees), gifts and income the member reported, and payments made at the member’s request. Those rows are listed with the excusal. A recusal notice is tied to an excusal when the same member filed it within 45 days and its description shares two uncommon words with the file’s title. Land-use excusals are counted as before: a roll-call row printed “Excused” for a member who voted on another land-use item at the same meeting. Public bodies are left out.
limits: Being connected is not being corrupt. A declared interest is one the official disclosed. An investment row does not say how large the holding is beside the company, and voting on a file that names a past gift-giver is not in itself a breach: whether a member had to step aside depends on amounts and timing that only the Ethics Commission can rule on. “Excused” is not a recusal: the roll call prints the same word for a member who is out of the room, and only a recusal notice on file says otherwise; a member may also have recused orally without filing a notice. Most final votes on money files are unanimous, so a yes vote says little about any one member. Roll calls are on disk for money files and for measures a lobbyist cited by file number, from 2015; other ordinances are still not covered. Name matching is exact, so interests held through differently named entities are missed. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).

What was declared, or the link on record
